text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VJESNIK

- Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and Bosnia's Alija Izetbegovic strike a deal during Wednesday's talks in Split to agree on the use of the Croatian port of Ploce and passage through the Adriatic resort of Neum within three months.
- Izetbegovic and Tudjman also plan to exchange a draft agreement on regulating relations between their two countries by September 1.
- Household electricity bills to rise by three percent.

- "The Hague tribunal has no evidence that (Bosnian Croat general Tihomir) Blaskic had ordered any attack on civilians," says Russel Hayman, one of Blaskic's defence counsels in the court. Blaskic has been indicted for war crimes against Moslem civilians in central Bosnia.

- Many Eastern Slavonian Serbs who could be candidates for the U.N. war crimes tribunal have fled the region after the U.N. captured and handed over Slavko Dokmanovic. One of the first to flee was Goran Hadzic, former president of the Serb para-state in Croatia.
- Seven houses set on fire near the Bosnian town of Jajce.

- By returning to Jajce en masse the Moslem side has violated all mutual agreements on organised returns, says Jajce Croat mayor Josip Lucic who says he is surprised at recent violence in the town since the relations between Moslem and Croats have been exceptionally good. He raises suspicion the incidents have been staged by a part of Moslem leadership.
- Germany suspended aid for rebuilding Jajce and asked other donor-countries to follow its example.

- Economic growth indicators for second quarter in 1997 show industry has recorded increasing demand but also a growing gap between orders for local and foreign markets. Construction work is on the rise.
VECERNJI LIST
- Tudjman has talks with American envoy Richard Holbrooke.
- Government prepares a law that would nullify legal acts now in force in Serb-held Eastern Slavonia. Length of service will be recognised, but court judgments will be revised.
- Banks are preparing to implement a new money-laundering law requiring them to identify persons carrying out transactions of 105,000 kuna and more.
- Trains between Beli Manastir and Osijek began on Wednesday after six years.
- Talks today over educational programme. Minister of education and sport meets UNTAES to discuss reintegration of Croatian schools.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA

- Privatisation Fund (HFP) will take offers for the sale of 51 holiday resorts on the coast, once owned by Serbian and Montenegrin state-run firms. One square metre will be roughly priced at some 880 German marks.

- Interview with HFP's deputy head Miljenko Weiss:"I am urging everybody to get vouchers. People first thought vouchers in the mass privatisation scheme could be exchanged for money immediately. That is not so, but in six months those shares could prove very lucrative."

- Stock Exchange: The central bourse in July recorded the biggest monthly turnover of 234 million kuna, up 49.08 percent from June. Average daily turnover totalled 12.3 million kuna. Monthly volume was put at 350,891 shares, up 43.26 percent from June. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-14557075
